div.head: Af 22
div.ab: XX. Gif mon on folces gemote cyninges gerefan geyppe eofot, ⁊ his eft geswican wille, gestæle on ryhtran hand, gif he mæge; gif he ne mæge, ðolie his angyldes.
XX. Gif mon on folces gemote cyninges gerefan geeofot yppe, ⁊ his eft geswican wille, gestæle on ryhtran hond, gif he mage; gif he ne mæge, ðolige his angildes, ond fó to ðam wite.
Be cynincges gerefan ðyfðe. Gyf mon on folces gemote cyninges gerefan geyppe þeofðe, ⁊ his eft geswican wille, gestǽle on rihtran hand, gyf he mæge; gyf he ne mæge, þolige his angyldes.

Si quis in populi conuentu preposito regis proclamationem ostendat (uel ostensionem denuntiet), et postea cessare uelit, pertrahat hoc ad rectiorem manum, si possit; si non possit, perdat suum angildum et reddat witam preposito.
[Be cynincges gerefan ðyfðe.] Gif mon on folces gemote cyninges gerefan geyppe eofot, ⁊ his eft geswican wille, gestæle on ryhtran hand, gif he mæge; gif he ne mæge, ðolie his angyldes.
{XX} Gif mon on folces gemote cyninges gerefan geyppe eofot, ⁊ his eft geswican wille, gestæle on ryhtran hand, gif he mæge; gif he ne mæge, ðolie his angyldes.

Wenn einer in der Volksversammlung dem Königsvogt [jemandes] Verschuldung [als Kläger] anzeigt, jedoch davon späterhin abstehen will, erhebe er die Klage gegen die richtigere Person, wenn er kann; wenn er [dies] nicht kann, gehe er seines Ersatzgeldes verlustig, (und [jener Vogt] erhalte [von ihm] das Strafgeld).

If someone in the public assembly reports [someone’s] offence to the king’s reeve [as plaintiff], but later wishes to withdraw from it, let him bring the charge against the more rightful person, if he can; if he cannot, let him lose his compensation-money (and let [that reeve] receive the fine [from him]).

If anyone makes an accusation [against another] at a public meeting, in the presence of the king's reeve, and afterwards wishes to withdraw it, he shall prefer the charge, if he can, against a more likely person. If he cannot he shall lose the value due to him.

If anyone brings up a charge in a public meeting before the king’s reeve, and afterwards wishes to withdraw it, he is to make the accusation against a more likely person, if he can; if he cannot, he is to forfeit his compensation.

If a person should reveal an offense to the king’s reeve in the folk assembly, and he afterwards wishes to withdraw [the accusation], let him accuse the correct party if he can; if he cannot, let him forfeit the single-payment [due him for the offense].

note.seg: ⁊ fó to ðam wite fügt zu So
⁊ fó to ðam wite added by So
so Lond; conv. publico statt po. co. übrige
thus Lond; conv. publico instead of po. co. the others
proclam. — wit. preposito skipped by K
‘Vom Diebstahl [gehörig zur Kompetenz samt Strafgeldempfang] eines Königsvogts’ Rb B
‘Of the theft [belonging to the jurisdiction, together with receipt of the fine] of a king’s reeve’ Rb B
= court; see that word in Gl 13

Über die Verderbnis, die Spätere am Worte cofot begingen, s. o. zu Af Rb 22. Toller nimmt zwar gecofot auf; es scheint aber unbelegt. Das Fem. für ‘Diebstahl’ passt nicht zu Af, wegen dessen his. — In Q ist Eingeklammertes uel o. d. wohl des Verfs. Korrektur

On the corruption that later writers inflicted on the word cofot, see above on Af Rb 22. Toller does admit gecofot; but it seems to be unattested. The fem. for ‘theft’ does not fit Af, because of Af’s his. — In Q the bracketed uel o. d. is probably the author’s correction

S. Gl Abfindung 1; Anzeige 13; Polizei 1a. Dem Sinne nach richtig ‘to conceal it’ Price, nur zu frei. Nicht immer lag die Absicht zugrunde, vom Verbrecher bestochen den Gerichtsherrn ums Strafgeld zu bringen. Denn unabsichtlichen Irrtum zieht in Betracht der Fall, wenn Kläger den Schuldigen nicht finden ‘kann’

See Gl Abfindung 1; Anzeige 13; Polizei 1a. ‘to conceal it’ Price, correct in sense, but too free. The underlying intention was not always to cheat the lord of the court of the fine, having been bribed by the criminal. For unintentional error is taken into account by the case where the plaintiff ‘cannot’ find the guilty party
Für erlittenen Schaden (nicht etwa ist dies an den Vogt zu zahlen); sy his spæce forloren III Atr 4, 2
For damage suffered (this is not, say, to be paid to the reeve); sy his spæce forloren III Atr 4, 2
Der Zusatz in H So Q stand wohl am Rande des Archetyps, ferner der zwei Urbilder unserer Hss., gls hbq, und endlich ihrer Ableitungen ls hb, und entging so E B Ld
The addition in H So Q probably stood in the margin of the archetype, then of the two exemplars of our MSS, gls hbq, and finally of their derivatives ls hb, and so escaped E B Ld
So Q; nicht ‘Kläger behalte [brauche nicht zu büssen]’. Ebenso III Atr 4, 2. Hn 24. 59, 27 (teilweise hierher)
So Q; not ‘let the plaintiff keep [need not pay compensation]’. Likewise III Atr 4, 2. Hn 24. 59, 27 (partly relevant here)
Welches eigentlich der Täter hätte zahlen sollen; Maurer Kr. Übsch. V 232. Vgl. Gl Klage 6—7e
Which the offender should properly have paid; Maurer Kr. Übsch. V 232. Cf. Gl Klage 6—7e

note.label: angyldes
note.seg: and fo to ðam wite. H.
H adds here ‘and he shall receive the fine.’ Presumably, the king’s reeve is the subject of the sentence, and the fine (for bringing a groundless accusation) must be paid by the plaintiff.

note.label: compensation
note.seg: Textus Roffensis adds: “and he [the reeve] is to succeed to the fine”
